content.text:
Copilot reported the following on setup.go:
maybePromptVercelDeploymentDisable hard-codes loading .entire/settings.json (settings.EntireSettingsFile) and later saves via settings.Save, so it will create/modify the project settings file even when the current flow is intentionally writing settings to settings.local.json (e.g., --local / determineSettingsTarget choosing local). This can unexpectedly create a committed settings file in “local-only” setups and is inconsistent with other settings updates in this file that respect opts.UseLocalSettings. Consider passing the intended settings target into this helper (or returning a desired change and letting the caller persist via SaveEntireSettings/SaveEntireSettingsLocal) so Vercel is persisted to the same settings file the command is managing, and update the output text accordingly.
I’m checking `setup.go` and the settings helpers to confirm how `maybePromptVercelDeploymentDisable` persists configuration and where it diverges from the rest of the setup flow.
I found the issue in `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`; next I’m tracing each caller to see whether the helper should save locally, save project-wide, or just return a mutation for the caller to persist.

The helper is directly loading and saving `.entire/settings.json`, and every caller currently ignores the setup target. I’m patching it to accept the intended settings destination and adding tests that cover the `--local` path.

I’ve identified one `enable` path that already tracks the resolved target and several reuse paths that should fall back to the existing file-selection logic. I’m updating the helper to accept that target explicitly and keep the no-flag behavior consistent.

I’m also checking the single-agent configure path, because if `--agent ... --local` still hard-saves project settings there, the Vercel fix should cover that path too rather than only the main interactive flow.

There’s a second inconsistency in the non-interactive `--agent` path: it always saves project settings and prints the project config path. I’m folding that into the same patch so the target file is consistent end-to-end.
I’m making the patch narrowly around settings-target selection and persistence, then I’ll run focused setup tests first before deciding whether a broader suite is warranted.

content.text:
Updated `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go` so Vercel persistence now follows the same settings target as the rest of the configure flow instead of always touching `.entire/settings.json`.

The change does three things:
- `maybePromptVercelDeploymentDisable` now accepts the intended settings target, loads that file, saves back to that file, and reports the correct path in its output.
- The main interactive setup flow passes its resolved target through, and the non-interactive `--agent` path now respects `--local` / `--project` for both saving and status output.
- Added a regression test in [cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-cli/cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go) that verifies Vercel config is written only to `.entire/settings.local.json` when requested.

Verification:
- `gofmt -w cmd/entire/cli/setup.go cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go`
- `env GOCACHE=/tmp/zeugs-gocache GOPATH=/tmp/zeugs-gopath go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run 'TestMaybePromptVercelDeploymentDisable|TestConfigureCmd_RemoveFlag_StillWorks|TestConfigureCmd'`
